title: Tangent fermions can restore vacuum stability of discrete-time Dirac models
abstract: The Dirac quantum walk (a 1+1 dimensional space-time discretization of the Dirac equation) has a $2μ$ mass gap both at the center and at the corner of the quasi-energy-momentum Brillouin zone. Gupta and Short recently noted [Quantum 9, 1845 (2025)] that the Dirac vacuum can create a particle-hole pair at the zone corner with the release of an energy $2μ$ to the environment. They removed this vacuum instability at the expense of fermion doubling, the appearance of a second low-energy Dirac cone. Here we show that an alternative discretization scheme, with a tangent rather than a sine dispersion relation, offers stability while retaining a single Dirac cone. The key step is the Cayley transformation from the unit circle of Floquet eigenvalues $e^{-i\varepsilon}$ to the real line of unbounded energies $E=2\tan(\varepsilon/2)$. We compute the Schwinger effect (particle-hole pair creation in a uniform electric field) for tangent fermions and show that the pair-production rate agrees with the continuum result for a single Dirac cone. The zone corner is exactly decoupled if the scalar potential is coupled through the Hermitian generator of the quantum map. If it is coupled as a split operator, in order to preserve exact gauge invariance on the lattice, the corner does contribute - with a weight that vanishes quadratically with the lattice constants, in contrast to the Dirac quantum walk where the zone-corner instability survives the continuum limit.
summary: This paper resolves a known vacuum instability issue in discrete-time Dirac models by proposing a tangent fermion discretization. The authors demonstrate that this new scheme maintains a single Dirac cone while ensuring that pair creation at the zone corner does not lead to vacuum decay in the continuum limit. This offers a stable lattice approach for studying relativistic quantum dynamics.
main_problem: The paper addresses the vacuum instability of the Dirac quantum walk in discrete time, which arises from particle-hole pair creation at the zone corner.
main_result: By employing a tangent fermion discretization scheme and using a symmetric split-operator coupling, the model restores vacuum stability by ensuring the zone corner remains gapless and decoupled from the energy release mechanism in the continuum limit.
method: The analysis uses the Cayley transformation to map quasi-energies to real energies and calculates the Schwinger effect (pair-production rate) by comparing different lattice coupling schemes.
model_or_system: The system is a Dirac quantum walk modeled by a discrete-time quantum map. The analysis compares the original Dirac quantum walk to a novel tangent fermion discretization, which is analyzed using Floquet operators and coupling potentials.
key_observables: Schwinger pair-production rate ($\kappa$), quasi-energy gap ($\Delta_\pi$), and the dispersion relation across the Brillouin zone corner.
important_parameters: Lattice constants ($	au, a$), mass gap ($\mu$), potential strength ($V_0$), and the smoothness parameter ($\lambda$).
main_assumptions: The analysis distinguishes between spatially-averaged and exactly gauge-invariant split-operator couplings, and examines the continuum limit ($	au 	o 0$).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the energy balance showing instability in the original model, the gapless crossing in the tangent fermion model, and the calculated pair production probability $T$ for different coupling schemes.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first identifying the instability in the standard Dirac quantum walk, then introducing the tangent fermion scheme, and finally performing a detailed comparison of coupling methods (gauge invariant vs. averaged) to show how the instability is suppressed or vanishes in the continuum limit.
why_interesting: The work provides a rigorous theoretical framework for stabilizing lattice discretizations of continuum physics (like the Dirac equation), which is crucial for developing reliable numerical simulations in condensed matter theory.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Quasi-energy–momentum dispersion relation (2.3) of the Dirac quantum walk (2.1), plotted for mass µ = 0.5/τ over several Brillouin zones. Black and white dots indicate filled and empty states, respectively. A particle-hole pair created at k = 0 consumes an energy 2µ, while at k = π/a it releases an energy 2µ. The energy balance can be understood as a temporal Umklapp process. While the periodic drive injects an energy 2π/τ in the system, the particle at k = π/a only gains 2π/τ −2µ.

FIG. 2. Dispersion relation (2.6) of the tangent fermion quan- tum map (2.4), plotted for mass µ = 0.5 and velocity v = 1. The mass does not open a gap at k = π, precluding the energy release process of Fig. 1.

FIG. 3. Dispersion relation (2.6) plotted for the Cayley energy E = 2 tan(ε/2), rather than for the quasi-energy ε (same parameters as in Fig. 2). The regions identified with the Fermi sea and the Dirac vacuum are indicated, as well as a particle- hole pair produced by interband tunneling (Klein tunneling) in the presence of an electric field F. The infinite band gap at k = π precludes the instability mechanism of Fig. 1 for the spatially-averaged coupling.

FIG. 4. Pair production probability T for the tangent fermion quantum map in a uniform electric field F, included via the spatially-averaged coupling. The data points are computed numerically by integration of the Landau-Zener Hamiltonian (3.6), the solid line is the small-F result (3.10).

FIG. 5. Pair production probability T0 at zone center and Tπ at zone corner, for the tangent fermion quantum map in a uniform electric field F, included via the split-operator cou- pling. The data points are computed numerically from the spectral flow equation (4.4), the solid and dashed lines are the small-F results (4.6) and (4.11), respectively. The error bars for Tπ give the standard deviation upon averaging over momentum sweeps in the interval π −δk < k < π + δk with δk ∈(0.8, 2.6). There is no significant sweep interval depen- dence for T0.
